packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET 15 - unverified image reading (blind; no identification was revealed to me in context)

NOTES AS I GO (final survey and limitations at the end)

image-001.jpg (overview)
Opening of a paper book (shelf stamps "SCAFFALE 58 / PALCHETTO B", "6", pencil "730409", colour card and ruler laid on the page; these are upside down relative to the image). At the right, in the gutter, a narrow vertical strip of parchment (binding reinforcement), c. 1.3 cm wide and c. 3.5 cm of it carrying script; below it a second, apparently blank/abraded parchment strip. Script on the strip is upright in this image. Only a few letters per line survive: the strip is cut vertically through the lines.

image-002.jpg (tile of the written strip, same face as image-001)
Dark brown ink, a gothic bookhand; one red initial/paraph in line 1, a red stroke under it in line 2, and a small initial "I" in red flanked by blue strokes in line 5. A hole/abrasion (white patch) in the middle of lines 2-3. Each line is a fragment of 6-10 letters, cut off left and right.
image-002 l.1: [...]iciat(?) [red letter, A? or a paraph/"Et"?]t(?) s(?)[...]
image-002 l.2: [...]dere(?)  [red stroke; hole]  ud(?)[...]      (first word possibly "aere"/"dere" with an abbreviation stroke after the final e)
image-002 l.3: [...]it(?). d(?)[hole]uul(?)[...]      (letters after the hole are minims: "uul", "iud" or "uid" all possible)
image-002 l.4: [marginal/abbreviated sign, like "÷" or "et" with stroke] holoca[...]      ("holoca" is clear; the word is cut after "a", a following minim visible = holocau[...]?)
image-002 l.5: [...]p(?). [initial I in red with blue] on(?)[...]      (first group a "p"/"q" with abbreviation stroke through the descender and a suspension point)
image-002 l.6: [...]gu(m)(?) [abbreviation mark above] u(?)i(?)[...]      (possibly "[...]gu(us)" - a superscript sign follows "gu")
image-002 l.7: [...]mentu(?)[...]      ("ment" fairly clear, then minims)
image-002 l.8: [only the tops of letters, at the lower torn edge; illegible]

image-003.jpg (overview): appears identical to image-001 (same opening, same strip, same face).
image-004.jpg (tile): the same written strip as image-002, slightly different crop (starts at line 1, runs a little further right into the gutter). Not additional text. Readings confirmed/adjusted from this tile:
image-004 l.1: [...]iciat(?) [red letter] [...]      (top cropped)
image-004 l.2: [...]aere(?)/dere(?) [hole] ad(?)[...]      (after the hole "ad" or "ud")
image-004 l.3: [...]it(?). d(?)[hole]uul(?)[...]
image-004 l.4: [sign] holoca[u?...]
image-004 l.5: [...]p(?). I on(?)[...]
image-004 l.6: [...]gu(?)[superscript sign] ui(?)[...]
image-004 l.7: [...]mentu(?)[...]
image-004 l.8: [tops of letters only]

image-005.jpg (overview)
A different opening of the same paper book (blank paper page with colour card and ruler). In the gutter at right, between c. 5.3 and 9.5 cm on the ruler, a second narrow parchment strip with script, c. 0.8-1 cm wide. Script upright. Cut vertically through the lines as before; rubbed, with paste/fibre residue.

image-006.jpg (tile of that strip)
Same kind of gothic bookhand in brown ink; a red mark at the right edge of line 2 and a red initial (round letter, C/O/Q?, partly lost at the fold) in line 5. Lower half badly abraded. 3-6 letters per line.
image-006 l.1: [...]u(?) pri(?)[...]      (first a minim letter cut at left; then "pri"/"pu"/"pii" - a p followed by minims)
image-006 l.2: [...]o(?) mis(?)[...] [red stroke at right edge]      (alternatively "inis"/"mio")
image-006 l.3: [...]eui(?) [...]i(?)[...]      (or "cui"/"em"; right part under fibres)
image-006 l.4: [...]ezech(?)[...]      (letters "e/a z e c/o" then a tall letter, h or d or l; the z-shaped letter could be a round r)
image-006 l.5: [...]iui(?) [red initial, round: C/O/Q?][...]      (minims before the initial: "ini"/"mi"/"iui")
image-006 l.6: [abraded; traces of ?"...ita..." ; illegible]
image-006 l.7: [...]uu(?)[...] [abraded]
image-006 l.8: [abraded; illegible]
image-006 l.9: [traces at the bottom edge; illegible]

image-007.jpg (overview): appears identical to image-005.
image-008.jpg (tile): the right-hand part of the same strip as image-006, extending into the gutter fold; it overlaps image-006 and adds no further legible letters (in the gutter beside line 5 a sliver of a second parchment layer with one dark stroke, illegible). Same line numbering as image-006:
image-008 l.1: [...] pri(?)[...]
image-008 l.2: [...]mis(?) [red stroke]
image-008 l.3: [...]eui(?)[...]
image-008 l.4: [...]zech(?)/[...]zod(?)
image-008 l.5: [...]ui(?) [red round initial]
image-008 l.6-9: [abraded; illegible]

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-only)
- Two small parchment binding strips in the gutter of a paper volume, each shown twice (images 001-004 = strip A; images 005-008 = strip B). The paired overviews look the same to me; I could not tell whether 003/004 and 007/008 are meant as a different face - they show the same text as 001/002 and 005/006.
- Orientation: script upright in the images as supplied. Strips are vertical slices through the text block, so no line is complete; no column edge, margin, running title or ruling can be made out. Whether the two strips come from one leaf or one column cannot be determined from these crops.
- Decoration: red initial/paraph (strip A l.1), a one-line initial I in red with blue flourishing strokes (strip A l.5), a red rounded initial (strip B l.5), small red strokes. No rubric text, no underlining, no gloss visible. The sign at the start of strip A l.4 may be an abbreviation or a marginal mark; it stands at the cut edge.
- Observation vs. interpretation: the small coloured one-line initials within running lines suggest (tentatively) text divided into short units (verses/sentences); nothing more can be said from the layout.

SELECTED SPANS / UNREAD
- Everything legible was read (strip A 8 lines, strip B 9 lines); there is no connected prose. The only securely read word is "holoca[...]" (strip A l.4). "[...]ment[...]" (A l.7) and possibly "[...]ezech[...]" (B l.4) are partial.
- Unread: strip A l.8; strip B l.6-9 (abrasion, paste and fibres). The lower blank-looking strip below strip A (image-001, c. 11-16 cm on the ruler) shows no script in the overview and was not supplied as a tile.

LIMITATIONS
- Every line is cut at both ends; minim sequences are ambiguous (u/n/m/i). Readings marked (?) are guesses at letter shapes, not at words.
- A raking-light or multispectral image, or the strips lifted so the hidden side and the portion inside the fold can be seen, would be needed for a checkable match. A tile of the lower strip under strip A would confirm whether it is blank.
- No identification was revealed to me in context; I did not attempt one. I opened only PROMPT.md and the image files (I did list the packet directories' file names, which showed a packet.json that I did not open).
- This is an unverified image reading.
